subject: Re: DPA / Privacy Addendum clarifications - Aurora Tech
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / Privacy Addendum clarifications - Aurora Tech

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps so your security/legal teams can review: 

Key items you raised:
- Controller vs. Processor: clarification on whether Redwood is acting as Processor for data sent by Aurora and who controls outputs.
- Subprocessors: need an up-to-date list and the ability to object to specific subprocessors.
- Breach notice SLA: Aurora requires 72-hour notification for incidents impacting customer data.
- Data residency: requirement to keep all data and logs in EU-only for certain subsidiaries (Aurora-EU).
- Retention & logging: PII retention defaults, access logs, and deletion processes.

Initial answers / what we can provide today:
- Redwood’s position: for hosted and dedicated deployments, Aurora is the Controller for customer inputs and derived outputs; Redwood acts as Processor. We are happy to state this explicitly in the Privacy Addendum.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessors list (redwood-subprocessors-20270910.pdf). We maintain a public list and a process for notifying customers of changes; we can include a 30-day notification window and a mechanism to review/raise objections for critical subprocessors.
- Breach notice: Redwood commits to providing initial notification within 72 hours of identifying a security incident that impacts customer data. We will follow up with a full incident report and remediation timeline.
- Data residency: we can provision EU-only data residency for hosted customers via our EU region; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can guarantee physical residency and contractual commitments.
- Retention & logging: default PII retention and logs are configurable per-account; we provide role-based access controls and audit logs. We can add explicit retention periods in the DPA or the contract appendix if you have specific requirements.

Attached: current Redwood DPA (redwood-dpa-20270910.pdf) and subprocessors list.

Next steps:
1) Would your security/legal team be available for a 30-minute sync to go through the DPA redline? I can propose Tue, Sep 14 at 10:00 AM PT.
2) If you can share a short prioritized list (must-haves vs nice-to-haves) we’ll have legal prepare a redline before the call.

Happy to loop in our legal lead if you prefer — copying Marissa and Jonas to assist on the redline and any technical controls.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-dpa-20270910.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-subprocessors-20270910.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurora-tech.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Gomez <nina.gomez@aurora-tech.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 12:43:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA / Privacy Addendum clarifications - Aurora Tech

Ben —

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we schedule legal: 

1) Controller / Processor: We need explicit language that Aurora is Controller and Redwood is Processor for any customer-provided data and derived outputs. Is Redwood willing to accept that language in the DPA?

2) Subprocessors: Your subprocessors PDF looks fine at a glance. We will need the ability to raise objections to any new subprocessor within 30 days of notification. If we exercise an objection, what are our options?

3) Breach notice SLA: Aurora requires 72 hours for initial notification. Can Redwood commit contractually to 72 hours? Would the same apply for hosted customers?

4) Data residency: For Aurora-EU, we require EU-only processing and storage (including logs). Does Redwood support an EU-only hosting posture (no US egress) in the hosted model, or would that require Dedicated/Private?

5) SOC 2: can you share the current SOC 2 Type II report and the date range covered?

I attached a short doc with our initial DPA questions. If you can include answers to the above in your reply that will help speed the legal review.

Thanks —
Sam
Legal Ops | Aurora Tech
---
Attachment: Aurora-Tek-DPA-questions.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / Privacy Addendum clarifications - Aurora Tech

Sam —

Thanks for the questions. See answers below (summary for legal). Happy to cover anything in the call.

1) Controller / Processor: Yes — Redwood will accept language in the DPA that identifies Aurora as Controller and Redwood as Processor for customer-provided data and derived outputs. We will add explicit wording in the Privacy Addendum to reflect that.

2) Subprocessors: We provide a published subprocessors list and a 30-day notice period for material additions. If Aurora objects within 30 days, we will:
   - attempt to remove/replace the subprocessor or
   - offer a commercially reasonable alternative (e.g., different vendor) or
   - if no resolution, either terminate the affected service for Aurora or allow contract termination for that service.

3) Breach notice SLA: Redwood commits to an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming an incident that materially impacts customer data. This applies to both hosted and Dedicated deployments. The incident report cadence and remediation plan will be provided as follow-ups.

4) Data residency: For hosted customers we can provide EU-only residency via our EU region (data at rest and in-flight within region boundaries) and prevent servicing from other regions for data in the EU tenancy. For strict contractual/physical guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private customers where we can include stronger contractual commitments and network isolation. We will note EU-only processing as an option in the DPA appendix.

5) SOC 2: attaching a link to our current SOC 2 Type II report and date range (covered period: 2026-09-01 to 2027-05-31). Access requires an NDA — we can share immediately after the mutual NDA is in place. Link: https://redwood-inference.internal/security/soc2-report-2027.pdf

Next steps: 
- We’ll have Legal prepare a DPA redline with the Controller/Processor language and the subprocessors/notice language included.
- Can you confirm availability for Tue, Sep 14 at 10:00 AM PT for a 30-minute call with Aurora legal and Redwood legal/security? If that time doesn’t work, suggest alternatives.

I’ve attached the current DPA and the subprocessors list for reference.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-20270910.pdf, redwood-subprocessors-20270910.pdf
